Overall a Underwhelming Experience: Much better Veggie Experiences are in HCM than HUM
Jan 2026 • Family
Visited on 24th January 26 for dinner.
We were promptly ushered in and had the registration completed and escorted to the Dining Area on the First Floor. Ground floor is full of merchandise.
Ambiance: unique, nice, elegant.
Service: courteous, warm.
Food: freshly made, just enough portions, multitude delicious options for Vegans. Rice portion is acutely low.
Savored, Dong Din Pineapple, Acerola, Sweet Leaves, Cam fig, ginger, basil seeds, Green curry, Dong Nai Rambutan Salad, Young Copra Panna Cotta, Pomelo sweet soup with Tra Vinh coconut blossom nectar, for a price of 1,009,260VND, which was truly not value for money from any perspective. Ginger is overpowering, needs a dash of sweetness.

We somehow had the underwhelming experience due to the following and would not recommend for next time:
Sincerely wish wait staff proactively inquired during the course of savoring the delicacies
Provided additional spoon to use desserts proactively without having to gain the attention( though not much crowd existed)
Engaged with the customer unobtrusively though
Cleared up the plates on the table and cleaned up the table, promptly
Presented the food course wise than just placing the whole order at once, though requested not to

We felt, that the service orientation needs to be improved, portion sizes can be enhanced by 25% and the prices can be moderated by 25%.

Billing was accurate; but again needs to gain the attention of the wait staff to get it done.
This was the only restaurant in our entire 3 weeks of Vietnam trip that has asked us to post a positive review on Google.
Overall just OK experience.

Guest Service Manager
Dear Mr./Ms. PavalikaV, 

Thank you sincerely for sharing your detailed feedback with us. 

While we are glad to know you appreciated the ambiance and the warmth of our team, we are truly sorry that your overall experience felt underwhelming, particularly in terms of service attentiveness and dining flow. 

We have carefully noted your feedback regarding the lack of proactive check-ins, the need to request basic tableware, delays in clearing the table, and the courses not being served as requested. These are essential parts of the Hum experience, and we regret that we did not deliver them consistently. We are reinforcing these service standards with our team to ensure better attentiveness and timing. 

We also appreciate your comments on portion sizes, flavor balance, and overall value, which have been shared with our culinary team for review. 

Regarding your note about being asked to leave a positive review, we sincerely apologize. Since the very beginning of Hum, we have upheld a strict principle that our team must never request or encourage reviews in any form. We believe all feedback should come entirely from our guests’ own experience, freely and voluntarily. If this occurred, we are taking it seriously and reinforcing this principle across the team. 

Although we have not been able to locate your visit details, we would truly appreciate the opportunity to learn more. Please feel free to reach out via email at xinchao@hum-dining.vn or message us on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/hum.vietnam/. 

Thank you again for your honest feedback. We hope to have the chance to welcome you back for a better experience.

Who would have thought you could deliver such delicious vegetarian food
Mar 2026 • Couples
We started our Ho Chi Minh visit when we literally stumbled upon this space with an abundance of atmospheric joy, gift shop, coffee shop and restaurants. 
Starting at the coffee shop and shop, visiting all 3 floors. Each experience first class. My first taste of Vietnam on this occasion was a Bung Mi with BBQ pork. 

However above all the Hum lounge, entirely vegetarian was outstanding and hence the separate review. 
I visited Hanoi 8 years ago and it was very difficult to find vegetarian food for my wife. This experience was off the scale wonderful. 
So good we visited twice, making a lunch before our journey home yesterday also. 
The menu is extensive and on the surface appears overwhelming. However I think whatever you choose would be of the highest quality. 
Staff were attentive and the value for money was incredible. 
It is in such lovely surroundings and the attention to detail is to be commended. Everything we ate was faultless. Even as a meat and fish lover I relished in trying as much as possible on the menu. 

Go and see for yourselves. An absolute must if you are visiting the city. 

I only wish I had the recipe for that Tom Yam!! If you are happy to share separately I would love to recreate.

Disappointing and over priced, style over substance
Jun 2025 • Couples
TLDR: Expensive, flavourless food in stunning settings. Avoid if you want modern plant based tastes.

As a vegan couple, we have eaten at a lot of veggie/vegan restaurants globally - from streetfood, to simple local eateries, to Michelin fine dining and everything in between.

The pros here are mostly around the architecture - a stunning building, beautiful interiors, and tranquil setting. The presentation of each dish is also wonderful, elegant and picture perfect. 

However the food itself was very disappointing. Much like vegan food's old reputation - before the welcome, plant-based revolution - it was bland, inspid, and flavourless. Interesting sounding vegetables and herbs brought little to the dish and tasted of less. No spice, no seasoning, no bursts of flavour. Not even any flavor from the interesting, fresh produce.

In the pickled kohlrabi and melon, the most flavoursome thing was the nicely massaged kale. The aubergine dish was also nice and pleasantly sweet. But the rest - packet style rice, English breakfast style mushrooms, egg roll - were forgettable before the plate was even cleared.

This was especially galling with the meal costing 3-5x anything else we've eaten in the city, very highly priced for the area, and being inarguably the least tasty meal we've had in Vietnam. And to top it all of, after five dishes (and 120k VND "health water" which was infused with fruit at a homeopathic level) we are writing this from a bahn mi spot because we were left hungry.

If, like the influencer live streaming her meal, you are interested in chic style over substance then you may love this - but if you're looking for bold flavour then steer clear.

If restaurants were just about
Jun 2020
If restaurants were just about food, this one would have all my stars. But they are not.
With automatic hand sanitizer at the front door, exquisitely decorated interior, tastefully lit and set tables the place feels and is high-end for Vietnamese (and other) standards.
Unlike many other places, HUM is sparkly clean, which is not the norm here. Waitresses are attentive, though English is sparse.
Food menu is lovely: always in good shape physically, with good descriptions and pictures. The best part is the food tastes and looks just as those appetizing pictures suggest. Every choice on the menu is tastefully presented and gives a lovely sampling of Vietnamese/Thai flavors. Yummy!
So if you are not a drinker and water is what gets you through, I can guarantee: you would leave 5-star struck.
Unfortunately I do like to accompany my restaurant experience with a sampling of their liquid menu choices. And here is how we lost one star down the drain... such a waste.
Cocktails: pictures in this case were much less helpful. House cocktails were lacking flavor and classic cocktails were just two shades under the standard. The classic vodka martini was small, poorly shaken (was not cold) and underwhelming; Cuba libre was unrecognizable and house choices were bland.
Onto wine: while the list had a number of offerings, the pricing of those choices was excessive, to be polite. Clearly, the wines selected were mostly to maximize the margin, rather than to pair with the gorgeous food offered (lack of pairing knowledge is a typical occurrence in Vietnam). Example: Matua Sauvignon Blanc (lovely wine) was 1.2m VND or 52USD per bottle, which is almost 3 times the retail price in town. Not good.
And then beer: Heineken and 333 in a can?? In a city that is buzzing with lovely microbreweries? Though I can only imagine an 8$ pint if it was on offer....
Anyway, the ambience and food are truly superb, service is good even with limited English, a nice place to visit. Just keep you pre-during-and-after drink expectations moderate.

For a dish that relies on texture, this is a miss. It's also salty. Portion is way too small. It's not good, but not too offensive. The crunchy house tofu is a total miss. The soft tofu is cut too thinly (almost French fries size) and the batter is too thick and chewy. Half way through the dish, the delicate tofu nearly disappeared as the batter hardened when cold. It's more fried dough and tofu. Really disappointing. The brown rice in lotus leaf is so so. Tiny portion. Green rolls (mustard leaf rolls - cuốn diếp) is bland. This is a classic rolls where the light bitterness of the young mustard leaves should be balanced out with sourness and saltiness. These rolls are totally bland except for the bitterness. Texture is also wrong with the occasional slimey bits of soft mushroom.

Nothing is authentic.

Now, the tea. There were 2 of us, and I ordered one cup of ginger tea. The waitress suggested a whole pot without telling us the price. I don't totally blame her on that because I should have asked. However in a country where teas are often offered for free with a full meal, or cost 5K VND a cup, this place charged about 130K VND. What's in the pot? Just ginger and the lowest grade tea. 

The bill comes with a 10% gratuity already included. This by itself is not a serious offense, but considering the general tipping culture in Vietnam at restaurant, this is almost an insult. Note that I always tip generously in places where this is common practice (underpaid waiters/tresses who relied on tip as main income like in the USA), but we feel that it shouldn't be forced on customers like this place. Note that services here are adequate, not exceptional (we asked for ice 4 times).

It's a great business decision to offer Vegetarian choice in this area, but food quality, service, pricing and portion are seriously lacking. For the price they charge, a slightly bigger portion won't hurt their profit. I won't be back.

We learnt from one of their waiters that the tofu was made fresh by the chef everyday! Being a huge fan of tofu, I really enjoyed the deep-fried tofu, spinach fried rice and the vermicelli hot-pot. The vermicelli hot-pot was cooked by one of the waiters on our table using a live-fire. I have yet to see any restaurant cook a hot-pot right in front of my eyes before, and I was really blown away by this! The food was mouth-watering and very appetizing, however we were too full to order desserts. We loved the food at Hum so much that we returned back for lunch once again before leaving HCMC. This time, we ordered our favourites and we also left some room for desserts and cocktails. We order the Mango Sticky Rice and the Fruity Milky Jelly to try, and I highly recommend the Fruity, Milky Jelly, especially on a hot day. The cocktails were very refreshing but they were not very strong in terms of the alcohol content, they tasted more like juice. I would highly recommend this restaurant to everyone to try at least once, whether or not you are vegetarian!

A gourmet recommended this restaurant for me and it was the best experience with vegetarian food I've ever had in my entire life in Saigon. 

Booking:
I called at 3pm, booked a table at 7pm. The staff was really supportive and saved me the most comfy place with sofa and near the window because I went there as couple.

Food:
Nice and clear pictures so you can have a full image of what you're about to have. Everything looked so beautiful that I wanted to try them all! Price range is around 65k-90k VND I ordered 4 dishes, 2 juices, 2 cocktails for 2 people. Everything was absolutely amazing that makes you forget that you're eating vegetarian food. Cooking style here is more like Thai food, but less spicy.

Service:
They close at 10pm, so last order is at 9:30pm. A staff will come and remind you to order desert or something else before 9:30 to make sure that they can serve you best. Of course you can stay longer than 10pm, maybe 10:30pm. But I don't agree when some customers complained about there closing time. They showed it very clear in the doorstep, you saw it, you're ok to come in and eat at their restaurant so you should at least respect their working time! Fair enough! If you want to stay until 23:30 or later, find yourself another restaurant and everybody will be happy!

Price:
We paid for whole dinner about 800k/2 ppl. My friends usually pay 900/3 ppl... so just for your reference. Of course the price is not included wine. 1 bottle was from 700k, by glass: 180k. I was so full that I didn't try desert. Next time then!

They have other branch in Saigon on Vo Van Tan st., but I haven't try it yet. Maybe I would go there for lunch with my colleagues. I highly recommend this restaurant for everybody!!!!
